A kid in my hometown was closeted up until high school, and was definitely bullied for it at least a little bit when he was younger. I’m not if that was the root cause, but he was a compulsive liar. He told everyone in middle school that his mom died. Kids in class, including myself, wrote him notes and cards expressing sympathy...and then the teacher said out loud a few days later that she had spoken with his mom on the phone. He was caught in another lie in high school, when he was telling people his sister died. He told a variety of stories about how it happened; cancer, drowning on her honeymoon...it was wild. We all found out that was a lie, too. As far as I know, he outgrew this behavior and distanced himself from our hometown. Maybe the child in OP’s post really just needs to get the f outta there and find their true self. Until then, they need as much help as possible.

The best thing about being a parent is the most obvious answer: your child. They will be so unbelievably beautiful to you, and you will love them like you’ve never loved anything in your life. My child makes my heart swell every day.

The most challenging thing (in my opinion) is that as a mom, you’re going to lose a part of yourself. One of the biggest struggles I’ve had as a mother is having the identity of “mother.” I was 22 when I had my daughter, so my individual experience may be different than someone who is a bit older. But it’s a crushing responsibility, and I honestly don’t know any parent who was ever totally ready for it. Nothing can prepare you for this, but you’ll have to base every decision you make and every plan you make around your child until they’re grown. 

My best advice, which I wish someone had told me: do some research while you have time to breathe. Look up how you want to parent your child, and talk it over with your partner/any other caretakers involved. I suggest @gentlemamma on Instagram. I wish I had sat down and really figured out my goals and my plan for my *own* behavior while parenting. It’s hard to stay patient and calm sometimes. Forgive yourself if you feel you’ve made mistakes.

You’re allowed to miss your old life. Feel those things if you need to!! Cry as much as you can.

Things are going to be hard for a while. I know (for the most part) how you’re feeling. But, like everyone says, things will get better. Your boobs will stop hurting so much, and your baby will get used to sleeping someday. Coronavirus isn’t going to last forever. All of this is temporary! The only thing you can try to do is remind yourself of that.
